items.title: Abbie Williams Interview, 1966-06-02
items.q: See, Said Frazier was my teacher.

ctx.x: You were talking about how drums were your craved, huh?

Yeah, yeah, I loved it. I loved the drums. I used to go to the Lyrics Theater and they had this guy, you're a red happy drummer. And this was my seat in the show, right by him. He had more runs than anybody in the world. And this guy, his brother, I played with him, Lil Jim, he died, bass drummer, Black Benny. I used to follow the parades. He was playing with Papa Celestan. And I used to carry his bass drum. And when they had a job, a parade when I'd leave, and from Chris Kelly, he had Faso and Mila Barnes was…
How old do you figure he was? Much older than you, huh?

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: Chani, now that's the original drummer from the Tuxedo Band, that's the original drummer.

ctx.x: We interviewed him a few months ago.

Chani, now that's the original drummer from the Tuxedo Band, that's the original drummer. Chani Bebe, because of his right name, his right name, I mean his nickname, we call his right name, Abbie William.
There were a few of the other drummers uptown, you remember a fellow by the name of Henry Zeno.
